reden: Yes. The audit report’s “[Medium] sqrt() high-exponent path halves an odd pre-exponent after incrementing it, giving a result off by 10x” is the same issue as the described [H-01]. Both point to Float128.sqrt’s large-exponent/Uint512 path where rExp is set (rExp = aExp - 72), then rMan is normalized (if rMan > MAX_L_DIGIT_NUMBER then rMan /= BASE; ++rExp), and only afterwards rExp is halved (rExp /= 2). Both explain this ordering causes the increment to be effectively lost due to integer division, yielding an exponent off-by-one and a result ~10x too small for certain large inputs (notably when the pre-halving exponent is odd / 73-digit case). Both propose equivalent fixes: perform the halving before the digit-adjustment, or equivalently add 2 before halving. Thus, same code path, same root cause, same impact, same specific fix.
